title: SaMo Bridge
description:
SaMo Bridge is a 24/7 respite hub for eligible people referred by the Santa Monica Police Department (SMPD). For those qualifying individuals experiencing homelessness, mental health or substance abuse problems, SaMo Bridge offers an opportunity to regroup and engage with an Exodus resource navigator who will help connect them with the supportive services necessary to get on the path to permanent housing and rehabilitation. 

For more information visit:  www.santamonica.gov/blog/samo-bridge-offers-participants-connection-resources-and-a-chance-at-a-new-path-to-recovery

I've been having problems with me using and I was out on the [music] streets and that I really needed help and I I don't want to go to jail because I was sick of going to jail also. They brought me to a hospital for uh 3 days to detox. Once a participant gets to the facility and they meet the criteria, they get linked with a navigator and a case manager. [music] The case manager is going to do a biocycle social screening form that's going to assess their immediate needs. [music] Once that's done, the participant will then get offered food, shower, and a lounger. We have 72 [music] hours to get these participants linked to immediate services. And then they're enrolled in the program [music] for 90 days. And during that 90 days, they're getting the services that they need. So again, mental health, substance abuse services, or even just housing. [music] Finally getting the experienced life sober, you know, being here, being present. Finally, it's it's a beautiful [music] thing. I I just really think that, you know, this should be in a lot of places. They have all these resources [music] for you. And, you know, I'm pretty much living proof, you know, from being a homeless person to finding finding help. People that work here, um, [music] at least a few of us have lived experience. Um, we know what it's like to be in jail. We know what it's like to [music] be homeless. Uh, we know what it's like to be addicted to drugs and have mental health, but we also know what it's like to come out of that. We know [music] what the struggle's like. To have somebody who's been there and has done that, it's all the more encouraging [music] for the individuals that are ready for help. Has helped us become successful is we're making sure [music] that we're not just connecting them to a service and then leaving them there. We're making sure that they're going to be linked up with somebody that's going to [music] continue the care that they need. >> We've had about 270 referrals from Santa Monica Police Department. [music] And from those referrals, we have over 200 that we've been able to service. We are [music] hitting our 6-month mark and we are looking to surpass that number within the first 6 months. So, we're really excited to [music] be able to show that this program is working and it's working quickly. We want folks to understand [music] that this is something that the community can see as an end to the cycle, right? folks who are picking up very low-level misdemeanor [music] citations, sleeping in doorways, camping. Those kind of citations are really rooted in homelessness, substance abuse, mental health. So these opportunity at Samo Bridge [music] to get immediately connected instead of just spending one more night in jail and getting immediately released. Samo Bridge is there to kind of connect them to that next step.
